subject: Unexpected invoice overage — request for usage breakdown and remediation
messages:
From: Maya Lopez <maya@atlasretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Retail Finance <finance@atlasretail.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected overage on May invoice (INV-2026-05-4178)

Hi Marissa,

We're reviewing our May invoice (INV-2026-05-4178) and seeing a $12,400 overage compared to our expected budget. Our engineering team reports no deliberate traffic increase during the billing window — the only notable activity was a staging migration on 2026-05-30.

Can you provide a detailed token/ingest breakdown for our account for May (preferably per-day and per-route), and any evidence of duplicate ingestion or retries that could explain the spike? We also need to understand whether any retry/replay behavior on our side could have been amplified by the Redwood SDK proxy rollout.

We'd like this by EOD Thursday so our finance team can close the month. If there's a clear platform-side cause, please advise on credits and next steps.

Thanks,
Maya Lopez
Head of Platform Operations
Atlas Retail
maya@atlasretail.com

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on May invoice (INV-2026-05-4178)

Hi Maya —

Thanks for flagging this. I understand the need for a fast, clear breakdown. I've looped in Ben from Billing/CS to help pull the per-route and per-day usage export and to investigate whether there were any platform-side events that could have caused duplication.

Planned next steps:
- Ben: generate raw usage export (CSV) for 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-31 with route-level and request-id columns.
- Internal triage: check for proxy-related duplicate request IDs or elevated retry counts around 2026-05-30.
- If we identify platform-induced duplication, we'll propose a remediation credit and outline mitigation.

I'll send a customer-ready summary once we have the export and preliminary analysis.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected overage on May invoice — preliminary analysis and evidence

Marissa / Rishi —

I've pulled the usage export and ran a short sampling analysis. Summary of findings:

- Total tokens billed (May): 4,920,134 (per invoice).
- Baseline expected tokens (historical median): ~3,100,000 — delta ~1.82M tokens.
- Spike window: 2026-05-30 03:00 — 2026-05-30 08:45 UTC. During this window we see a ~6x increase vs same window previous week.
- Duplicate request-id pattern: roughly 14% of POSTs to the /v1/ingest endpoint during the spike share identical request_id and identical payload checksums across multiple events (indicative of retries being accepted as distinct writes).
- Root cause hypothesis: A Redwood SDK proxy patch (deployed 2026-05-30 02:55 UTC) changed retry semantics for certain CONNECT timeouts, causing client retries to be forwarded without de-duplication headers in some edge cases. The proxy should have added an X-Redwood-Idempotency header; in ~14% of observed events it was missing due to a race in the initialization path.

What I attached:
- usage-export-2026-05-31.csv (route, timestamp_utc, request_id, token_count, checksum)
- duplication-sample-analysis-2026-06-04.pdf (short write-up + sample rows showing repeated request_ids and payload checksums)

Recommended customer-facing remediation:
1) Offer a pro-rated credit for duplicated tokens during the spike window. Our sample analysis estimates duplicated tokens at ~1.1M tokens (we considered only exact-request-id duplicates with identical checksums).
2) Commit to a technical mitigation: immediate proxy rollback patch and an idempotency enforcement rule at the ingest edge to reject exact-duplicate request_ids within a 24-hour window.
3) Provide the CSV and the analysis to Atlas so they can confirm on their side.

Proposed credit calculation (conservative): 1.1M tokens * $0.0008/token = $880 credit. This is conservative relative to the full delta vs baseline. Recommend we present this as an account credit or invoice adjustment — whichever they prefer.

Let me know if you'd like me to send the summary to Maya and Finance or if you want to review first.

Ben Carter
Billing Lead, GTM Finance — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: usage-export-2026-05-31.csv (CSV, 2.1 MB); duplication-sample-analysis-2026-06-04.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Lopez <maya@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Atlas Retail Finance <finance@atlasretail.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on May invoice (INV-2026-05-4178)

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for raising this. I've attached the raw usage export and a short analysis from our billing team that shows the likely source of the overage. Key points:

- We observed a concentrated spike on 2026-05-30 between 03:00–08:45 UTC that accounts for the majority of the additional tokens.
- Our analysis found repeated request_ids with identical payload checksums in ~14% of requests during the spike window, consistent with retries being forwarded as new writes.
- We have a patch ready to enforce idempotency at the ingest edge; we will deploy the rollback/patch by EOD Monday to prevent recurrence.

Proposed remediation:
- Redwood proposes a conservative credit of $880 applied to your June invoice (or as an account credit, whichever you prefer). This is based on a conservative estimate of 1.1M duplicated tokens and our current published rate.
- If you’d like a deeper reconciliation, Ben can walk through the CSV and sample rows with your engineering team.

Next steps: please confirm if you'd prefer an invoice adjustment or an account credit, and whether you'd like a quick 30-minute sync to walk the data with Ben and our infra engineer.
